\newcommand{\exText}{We check the solutions against exact profit maximisation in two ways. First, with no weight on the future and juniors treated alike, short-horizon hiring in each year solves the first-order condition of Corollary~\ref{cor:static}, or is zero if the juniors carried over already exceed the level it implies. Re-solving the projected-scenario paths year by year in this way with the exact $\Pi^*$ reproduces hiring to within 0.15\% of the usual intake in every year in both sectors, gives the same years of zero hiring, and changes the year-44 senior stock by less than 0.01. Second, along both firms' paths in years 5 to 44 the approximation's relative error in $\Pi^*$ is below 0.005\% and its error in $\partial\Pi^*/\partial\hat A$ below \$1.1k a year, against a junior wage of \$372k in law and \$345k in banking. Only the short-horizon paths can be re-solved exactly in this way; errors away from the solution paths are reported under Numerics in Appendix~\ref{sec:limits}.}
